text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with two changed-quantity, two reordered and two moved-negation quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the volunteer orientation for the Kirembe District Household Health Programme. Each community health worker will be responsible for visiting 40 households every month, and you should record every visit in the green register before the end of the day. Volunteers are not expected to diagnose illness, but they are expected to recognise danger signs. You may give oral rehydration salts, but you must not give antibiotics without a nurse's approval. In 2022, volunteers who completed all three refresher sessions identified 65% more pregnant women for antenatal referral than those who missed training. If a child has a fever lasting more than two days, refer the family to Ngaro Health Centre immediately. Never ask a family for payment; the Mvuli Community Health Trust covers your transport allowance of 3,000 shillings per week.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2023, the Sanko Valley School Meals Initiative served a hot midday meal in 28 primary schools across Bendara Region. Field monitors visited every school at least twice and found that attendance on meal days averaged 91%, compared with 74% on days when deliveries failed. Cooks did not receive the fortified oil consignment in August, so meals in nine schools lacked the planned vitamin A content. Parent committees contributed firewood and water, but they were not asked to pay cash. Not all storage rooms were rodent-proof, and in four schools monitors found sacks of grain stacked directly on the floor. The programme reached 11,400 pupils, slightly below the target of twelve thousand.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation covers the first eighteen months of the Lamplight Evening Literacy Network, which runs 46 classes in community halls across the Orvane and Delmira districts. Of the 1,120 learners enrolled in March 2022, 812 were still attending at the evaluation point, a retention rate of 72.5%. Facilitators reported that women attended more regularly than men, although men did not drop out because of the timetable. Most learners could not read a short public notice at intake; by month twelve, 58% could do so unaided. The evaluators did not find evidence that the mobile phone lessons improved writing more than reading. Classes held after 8 p.m. were less popular, and two halls had no reliable lighting.

passages.source_passage: Background. Kassala Ridge camp, established in 2016, now hosts approximately 38,000 refugees, of whom nearly half are under eighteen. The Harbourlight Protection Collective has provided case management in the camp since 2019, referring medical cases to the Tessaly Clinic, but current staffing allows only six caseworkers to cover four residential blocks. In the last year, caseworkers opened 1,450 new files, and 30% involved survivors of gender-based violence. Many survivors did not report incidents because the only reporting desk was not staffed at night. No dedicated safe space exists for adolescent boys, and unaccompanied children are not always registered within the 72-hour standard. This proposal requests funding to recruit additional caseworkers and to extend reporting hours.

passages.source_passage: Between January and June 2024, the Clearbrook Rural Water Partnership completed 14 of the 20 boreholes planned for Mitende sub-county. Water quality tests at all completed sites met national standards, although two boreholes did not yet have functioning hand pumps. Household latrine coverage rose from 41% to 63% in the six target villages. Monitors noted that girls avoided latrines without doors more often than boys, and that handwashing stations were never refilled in eleven households visited. Water committees collected user fees in five villages but kept no written accounts. The drilling contractor was not able to reach the hilltop site at Kerebu during the rains, and work there will resume in September.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Safe Hearth Family Reunification Service reviewed case files for the period from April 2022 to September 2023. During this time, 214 separated children were placed with trained foster carers, and family tracing teams located relatives for 131 of them. Reunification was not attempted until a home assessment had been completed, which evaluators considered good practice. However, follow-up visits after reunification did not happen within the required three months in about a quarter of cases. Foster carers said they were never told how long a placement would last. Children over fourteen were consulted more consistently than younger children, and no child was reunified against their stated wishes.

passages.source_passage: At the midpoint of its five-year cycle, the Becas Luna Girls' Scholarship Programme supports 350 girls in lower and upper secondary schools in the highland departments of Valle Seco and Tierra Alta. The evaluation found that 89% of scholars progressed to the next grade in 2023, compared with 67% of non-scholar girls in the same schools. Scholars who failed a term were not removed from the programme but were offered tutoring, and the transport stipend meant most no longer walked two hours each way. Teachers did not observe a change in classroom participation, but parents did. Dropout was highest among girls who married early, and the programme has not yet developed a re-entry pathway for young mothers.

passages.source_passage: Background and rationale. Malaria remains the leading cause of outpatient visits in Ombeli Province, accounting for 38% of clinic consultations in 2023. The last mass distribution of insecticide-treated nets took place in 2020, and a household survey by the Restwell Malaria Initiative found that only one in three nets was still in usable condition; damaged nets were not replaced by households but were repurposed for gardens. Children under five were less likely than adults to sleep under a net. Fishing camps along the Tumba River were not reached in 2020, although they were included in household registers. We propose to distribute 96,000 nets through health clinics and to run hang-up visits through 240 school volunteers.

variants.moved_negation_2: damaged nets were replaced by households but were not repurposed for gardens.

passages.source_passage: The Little Steps Playgroup Network operates 62 community playgroups in the Marrow Hills area, each meeting three mornings a week for children aged three to five. By the mid-term point in October 2023, 1,870 children were enrolled, against an end-of-project target of 2,400. Caregivers who attended at least six parenting sessions reported reading to their children more often, although fathers did not attend sessions but did join home visits. Developmental screening showed gains in language, but not in fine motor skills. Volunteer facilitators were not paid in cash but were given food parcels, and turnover reached 35% in the first year. Several playgroups had no outdoor space, so active play was replaced by singing.

passages.source_passage: Facilitator notes, Session 4: Soil and Water. Each farmer field school in the Teshwe Valley network has between 20 and 25 members, and this session should last no longer than three hours. Begin at the demonstration plot, not in the meeting shed, so farmers can compare the mulched rows with the bare rows. In last season's trials, mulched plots yielded 30% more maize than unmulched plots, even though they received no extra fertiliser. Do not tell farmers which method is better, but do ask them to measure soil moisture. Women members should not be seated at the back but should lead the measurements. Remind the group that the Greenfurrow Farmers' Association will supply seed only to schools that have submitted their 2024 planting records.
